statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low while Stress remains extreme.
recommendation: Tail remains below the watch threshold. Delayed NQ references do not establish persistent one-way structure, while Broadcom guidance and the U.S.-Iran/Hormuz energy backdrop preserve extreme event stress.
headline: Low Tail risk with extreme event stress ahead of the September 3 U.S. data cluster
body: Public delayed NQ references are inconsistent, ranging from modestly negative to near flat, so current persistent price-path evidence is not reliable. Broadcom’s softer Q4 revenue guidance and renewed U.S.-Iran/Hormuz disruption keep technology, energy and rates transmission risk elevated.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 UTC clock hours, published Tail ranged from 18% to 31%. Orange states appeared at 04:00, 05:00, 07:00, 10:00, 11:00 and 12:00 UTC on September 2; the 22:00 UTC slot was unavailable. The latest published 00:00 UTC slot was green at 19% Tail, with Stress remaining extreme.
outlookSummary: The next concentrated risk window is 12:15-14:45 UTC on September 3 around the 12:30 UTC trade/productivity/claims/Waller cluster, the U.S. cash-open transition and 14:00 UTC ISM Services. Forecast Tail stays at or below 24% before outcomes because event importance alone does not establish persistent mean-reversion failure.

forecast.analysis: Delayed public NQ pages are inconsistent, ranging from modestly negative to near flat, so no reliable persistent one-way path is established. Broadcom’s softer Q4 revenue guide and elevated oil/Hormuz risk keep Stress extreme while Tail remains low.

forecast.analysis: If overnight NQ remains two-sided and meaningful retracements continue, Tail would stay low; repeated extension toward a session extreme with shallow pullbacks would be the main escalation signal.
In thin Asian-session liquidity, a balanced range would keep Tail low. A clean directional break would need confirmation from retracement quality rather than the size of a single move.
With no scheduled U.S. catalyst in this hour, risk would ease if price discovery stays rotational. A fresh geopolitical shock or abrupt rates impulse could restore event/whipsaw conditions.
Approaching Europe, cross-asset direction may become more informative. Tail would remain low unless NQ begins repeated extension and pullbacks fail to regain prior range.
European participation could widen ranges. Mixed equity behavior with retracements would preserve low Tail; synchronized technology weakness and rising yields would raise path risk.
At the Europe transition, NQ holding away from extremes with recurring pullbacks would keep the low-Tail baseline. Persistent alignment across semiconductors, rates and volatility would challenge it.
European cash trading may sharpen direction. Tail reaches watch only conditionally if NQ holds near an extreme and retracements become shallow or fail while cross-assets align.
With U.S. data still several hours away, watch-level Tail reflects the possibility of positioning pressure. A rotational range would favor a lower reading rather than sustained escalation.
Pre-U.S. positioning could increase directional efficiency. Tail remains conditional on whether any move extends after failed retracements, not on the upcoming releases themselves.
The approach to the 12:30 UTC release cluster raises event sensitivity. Tail stays below the block threshold unless price structure becomes persistently directional before the data.

The 12:30 UTC trade, productivity, claims and Waller cluster is a high-volatility checkpoint. Event importance raises Stress; Tail would require observed post-release extension with poor retracement quality.
drivers: 12:30 UTC trade, productivity and claims releases

forecast.analysis: The U.S. cash-open hour follows the 12:30 UTC data cluster. Tail remains at watch in the forecast unless opening-auction continuation holds near an extreme and pullbacks repeatedly fail.
drivers: U.S. cash open after the data cluster

forecast.analysis: ISM Services is scheduled for 14:00 UTC. The forecast keeps Tail at watch because a release is not itself evidence of mean-reversion failure; post-release structure would determine any escalation.
After ISM, an orderly two-way response would lower Tail from the event peak. Persistent same-direction extension across the cash session would keep the watch state elevated.
As the first post-data hour matures, retracement depth and breadth would matter more than the headline surprise. Normalization in yields or volatility would favor lower Tail.
Mid-session risk would ease if NQ rotates back through prior ranges. A one-way semiconductor-led move with shallow pullbacks would preserve watch-level path risk.
Later U.S. trading would remain sensitive to energy and rates. Tail would fall if cross-assets decouple and price action becomes two-sided; aligned extension would keep caution elevated.
Approaching the afternoon, the baseline is mixed. Continued retracements would argue against pathological persistence even if realized volatility remains high.
If the session has stayed rotational, Tail would return to low despite elevated macro Stress. A late-session break holding at an extreme would be the key contrary condition.
Power-hour structure would be assessed conditionally: balanced breadth and pullbacks would keep Tail low, while a late one-way extension could lift it back toward watch.
Near the cash close, orderly price discovery and fading volatility would keep Tail low. A closing-auction continuation without retracement would be the principal escalation case.
After the U.S. close, thinner liquidity could amplify headlines but would not by itself imply persistent Tail. Broadcom read-through and geopolitical developments remain conditional drivers.
Into the next UTC day, overnight conditions would remain mixed. The following day’s U.S. employment report raises background Stress, but Tail still depends on observed price-path persistence.

forecastDetail.comment: Current delayed NQ references do not reliably establish persistent one-way structure; Broadcom and energy/geopolitical catalysts keep Stress extreme.
Overnight Tail remains low if retracements persist; repeated extension with shallow pullbacks would be the escalation signal.
Thin Asian liquidity favors a low-Tail baseline unless a directional break is confirmed by poor retracement quality.
Without a scheduled U.S. catalyst, rotational price discovery would keep Tail low; headline or rates shocks remain the main exceptions.
Approaching Europe, Tail stays low unless NQ begins repeated extension and failed pullbacks.
European participation may widen ranges; synchronized technology weakness, higher yields and weak retracements would raise path risk.
